what_happened: Live-tested POST /v1/cli/context (the actual UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse hook endpoint) with project=nvim vs a nonexistent sentinel project; got byte-identical responses, reproducing the seed report's exact false claim ('90 tasks across 10 topics') live inside this repo. This directly answers the seed report's open research question (does the hook endpoint honor project=) rather than inferring it from the unrelated /v1/search endpoint, and forecloses the client-wrapper-filtering lever by test.

Dispatch description's §3 claimed 'two of the three hooks ... transmit the asking repository', citing sapience_cli.py:457/466 for the session and prompt branches. Corrected during research: the deployed SessionStart hook is python3 mcp.py --briefing-text (a different vendor script), which calls GET /briefing + GET /v1/outstanding with no project/cwd parameter at all -- the sapience_cli.py 'session' branch cited is dead code for this repo's actual wiring. Only one of three hooks (UserPromptSubmit) sends a project id, and sapience_cli.py/mcp.py both self-update daily so the cited line numbers had already drifted (457/466 -> 599/605).

Plan phases were partitioned so that suite_selection_select's union output over each phase's Files to modify paths could be run and quoted verbatim in Tier Justification; all four phases resolved to __FULL_SWEEP__ or an explicitly named check, so no suite name had to be guessed.

The dispatch description's 'two of the three hooks transmit the asking repository' figure is wrong (it is one of three: SessionStart runs mcp.py --briefing-text, a different vendor script that sends no body). Research corrected it; the plan carries the correction explicitly rather than the description's figure.

verify-sapience-context-scoping.sh's two-call project= comparison is not perfectly deterministic in a busy vault: 3 consecutive runs gave RESIDUAL_HOLDS, RESIDUAL_HOLDS, RESIDUAL_LIFTED, with the one differing run showing one extra rule item on the sentinel-project call rather than a systematic project-based filter effect. Likely cause: concurrent vault writes from sibling tasks in this same multi-task /orchestrate batch landing between the two calls, or server-side ranking jitter -- not evidence the vendor ask has landed. The probe's own RESIDUAL_LIFTED wording already says 'may have landed... re-verify before relying on this alone', and Phase 4's live-run interpretation should sample more than once before concluding either way.
